articles.title: WPL 2027 Auction: 146 players, including 119 Indians, to go under the hammer for 27 slots in Kochi
articles.summary: The highly anticipated player auction for the 2027 Women's Premier League is scheduled for October 28 in Kochi. A diverse pool of 146 cricketers, featuring 1...
articles.body:
The race to secure the remaining spots for the 2027 Women's Premier League (WPL) season will intensify at the player auction in Kochi on October 28, with 146 cricketers set to go under the hammer for just 27 available slots across the five franchises. England batter Sophia Dunkley and Australia all-rounder Sophie Molineux headline the auction pool with the highest base price of Rs 50 lakh. According to a WPL press release, the auction list features 119 Indian players, including 22 capped and 97 uncapped cricketers, alongside 27 overseas players, comprising 14 capped and 13 uncapped names. Six overseas players represent Associate Nations. Of the 27 slots available, 20 are reserved for Indian players and seven for overseas recruits. The auction is scheduled to begin at 5:30 PM.

Dunkley, Molineux lead highest base-price bracket

Dunkley and Molineux have registered at the top base price of Rs 50 lakh, putting the England batter and Australia all-rounder among the headline names in the auction. India's G Kamalini and Kiran Navgire, along with Australia's Heather Graham and Jess Jonassen, have set their base price at Rs 40 lakh. Another 30 players have registered in the Rs 30 lakh bracket. With limited vacancies across the five franchises, teams will need to balance their remaining budgets and squad requirements while identifying players who can strengthen their line-ups ahead of the new season.

Mumbai Indians acquire Tara Norris in trade

Ahead of the auction, Mumbai Indians acquired USA left-arm seamer Tara Norris from UP Warriorz at her base price of Rs 10 lakh. Norris previously represented Delhi Capitals in the inaugural WPL season in 2023, making an immediate impact by becoming the first bowler in the tournament's history to take a five-wicket haul. She returned figures of 5/29 against Royal Challengers Bengaluru at the Brabourne Stadium, dismissing Ellyse Perry, Heather Knight and Richa Ghosh among others. Her move to Mumbai adds another option to the franchise's bowling resources ahead of the auction. With 146 players competing for 27 places, the Kochi auction will offer franchises a final opportunity to address gaps in their squads and build combinations for the 2027 WPL season.

articles.title: Falcons head coach shares update on rookie LB Kendal Daniels
articles.summary: Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski shares positive update on rookie LB Kendal Daniels
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons lost starting linebacker Kendal Daniels to a neck injury during Sunday's 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears . Daniels was down on the ground for several minutes in a scary moment at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

Both teams sat in silence as the medial staff tended to the injured rookie. Daniels was eventually carted off and taken to a local hospital for further evaluation.

According to Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski, Daniels is out of the hospital and has returned to the team facility.

"All positive news on Kendal Daniels," Stefanski said during his Monday press conference. "He's here back in the building today. He got back from the hospital to the locker room after the game. So I feel very, very fortunate that he got the treatment that he got, but also we feel really good about where he is."

Daniels has been an incredible asset to Atlanta's defense this season. The fourth-round pick out of Oklahoma won the starting job out of training camp and hasn't looked back. Stefanski did not have an update on Daniels' status for the team's Week 7 game against the San Francisco 49ers.

"I have no updates really on Kendal for this game, or really anybody yet. Still working through imaging and those types of things on a bunch of guys but we'll work through that this week."

Assuming Daniels is out for Sunday's game, the Falcons would look to rookie linebacker Harold Perkins Jr. The sixth-round pick out of LSU has played well this season and should have no trouble stepping up.

Regardless of Daniels' status for Week 7, it's good to hear that he is out of the hospital and feeling better.

articles.summary: PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy hopes to have DeShon Elliott back this Sunday against the New Orleans […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy hopes to have DeShon Elliott back this Sunday against the New Orleans Saints.

McCarthy didn't have much of an update regarding the veteran safety, however.

"I thought he had a great week last week, so those are the conversations that we're having," McCarthy said during his weekly press conference on Monday afternoon at the UPMC Rooney Sports Complex.

Elliott returned to practice for the Steelers before their Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, having had his 21-day window opened. Elliott had been placed on injured reserve on cutdown day.

Elliott missed over half of last season with a significant hamstring injury suffered in October. He aggravated the injury after returning to action during the preseason. Elliott talked about the emotions that went into getting back on the field after the exhibition against the New York Jets.

"The first drive, I was rusty as hell," Elliott said. "I gave up a third-and-6 to the tight end. I had a lot of pregame jitters. First game back from the injury. Last time I played football, my dad was alive still, so it was a lot of emotion for me."

Alan Saunders provided reporting from Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Rams must prioritize Tutu Atwell being on the field!
articles.summary: The data shows that the Rams offense is more explosive with Tutu Atwell on the field
articles.body:
Tutu Atwell needs to be on the field more often if the Los Angeles Rams want their offense to become more consistent from drive to drive. With Davante Adams suffering an injury late in the Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the door is open for Atwell to earn a significantly larger role in Sean McVay's offense.

The Rams have struggled to find consistency throughout their 2026 campaign, and getting Atwell more involved would provide a much-needed spark. While Puka Nacua and Adams have commanded much of the attention in the passing game, Atwell possesses the speed and downfield ability to stretch opposing defenses in ways that can create opportunities for the entire offense.

Atwell's biggest value comes from his ability to threaten defenses vertically. His speed can force opposing cornerbacks to respect the deep ball, potentially opening up underneath routes for Nacua, Adams when healthy, and the Rams' tight ends. Los Angeles needs to find more ways to manufacture explosive plays rather than relying on the same targets throughout every possession.

And the data clearly shows that the Rams offense is more explosive when Tutu Atwell is on the field. At the very least, Tutu Atwell should be on the field for every obvious 3rd down passing situation.

Adams' late-game injury against Arizona makes that opportunity even more important. Depending on the severity of the injury and his availability for Week 7, Atwell could see an expanded snap count and more opportunities to establish himself as a reliable contributor. Even if Adams returns quickly, the Rams should consider giving Atwell a more consistent role.

The Rams cannot afford to let their offensive personnel become predictable, particularly as they attempt to climb back into contention in the NFC playoff picture. Rotating Atwell into more offensive packages could give quarterback Matthew Stafford another weapon capable of changing the complexion of a drive with one play.

Atwell does not need to replace Adams' production entirely to make a difference. He simply needs more opportunities to use his speed and create separation. If the Rams want a more explosive and dependable offense, getting Atwell involved should be a priority moving forward.

articles.title: How Jamel Dean's inside knowledge saved the Steelers in Tampa
articles.summary: James Harrison and Joe Haden praise Jamel Dean for using his inside knowledge of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to secure a clutch Steelers win.
articles.body:
When the Pittsburgh Steelers pulled off an emotional comeback victory in Tampa, star names like Aaron Rodgers and Jalen Ramsey naturally captured the headlines. However, the true unsung hero of Pittsburgh's late-game defensive stand was former Buccaneers cornerback Jamel Dean.

Returning to face his former team, Dean delivered a lockdown masterclass, utilizing his intimate familiarity with Tampa Bay's offensive scheme to make game-altering plays when the stakes were highest.

Dean spent significant time in Tampa's secondary, and that preparation paid massive dividends on Sunday. On the afternoon, he posted a stat line that read like a defensive coordinator's dream: six pass defense breakups, four tackles, and a crucial interception returned 40 yards that flipped the game's momentum. His instincts in high-stress third- and fourth-down situations kept the Buccaneers from extending drives down the stretch.

On the latest episode of the " Deebo and Joe " podcast, former Steelers legends James Harrison and Joe Haden broke down film of Dean's performance, praising his meticulous preparation and route recognition.

"My man Dean, what was that? Six passes defended, a interception, 40-yard return on that, and four tackles," Harrison noted, highlighting how Dean sat on route concepts before Tampa's receivers could make their breaks. "He was sitting on everything. It was like he knew their playbook. That man got good notes. Seven years over there, man. Got great notes."

Haden echoed Harrison's praise, detailing how Dean executed situational football flawlessly during crunch time. "Dean straps on second down. It's third and long. Play deep. Make them throw the ball in front of you. Catch and tackle."

Though Harrison jokingly criticized Dean for not tucking his shoulder on his 40-yard interception return to score, noting he "wouldn't have been out at the three," Dean's secondary execution was paramount. His masterclass against his former squad proved that preparation and inside knowledge can be just as lethal as raw talent.

articles.title: Jim Nantz hurts himself trying a football move on JJ Watt during Bills-Raiders broadcast
articles.summary: While calling the NFL’s Buffalo Bills-Las Vegas Raiders game for CBS, Jim Nantz hurt his hand with JJ Watt while trying to punch the football out of his hand...
articles.body:
While calling the NFL's Buffalo Bills-Las Vegas Raiders game for CBS, Jim Nantz hurt his hand with JJ Watt while trying to punch the football out of his hand.

Some of the benefits of watching a broadcast are the anecdotes and demonstrations. Watt held the football as Nantz tried to "peanut punch" it out .

This amused Watt, who didn't expect Nantz to try so hard. However, Nantz's efforts, which might have been admired, might've come at a cost. He joked that he broke his wrist.

Maybe this will be the first of many memorable moments with Nantz and Watt. Watt is CBS' replacement for Tony Romo this season, who was arrested for an OWI over the summer .

The Bills and Raiders faced off in an entertaining afternoon game on CBS in Week 6. Going into the fourth quarter, the Bills were up by 10 points. It looked like all hope was lost, but Kirk Cousins led his team down the field for a field goal.

This cut the lead down to seven points. The Raiders forced Josh Allen's offense to punt on their next drive, and Cousins threw a touchdown pass on their next offensive possession to tie the game.

However, it was all downhill from there. Allen led the Bills on a touchdown that chewed up over three minutes of the clock. Vegas got the ball with a chance to match the score, but Cousins was unable to complete a pass on the drive. The Bills scored another field goal on their next drive.

Cousins was able to connect with Tre Tucker on a deep touchdown pass on the Raiders' last drive to cut the lead to three, but they couldn't recover the ensuing onside kick.

articles.title: Jake Bauers vs. Blake Snell: A Breakdown
articles.summary: Breaking down the actual best at-bat of the NLCS
articles.body:
Last week, I wrote an article breaking down NLCS MVP Jake Bauers' 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto. At the time, I called it "the best at-bat of the NLCS."

That turned out to be incredibly presumptuous: just two days later, he worked an 11-pitch at-bat against Blake Snell that ended not with a walk, but with a go-ahead two-run home run.

Since the first at-bat earned a breakdown, this one deserves one too.

Snell doesn't have quite the pitch variety Yamamoto does, but the two-time Cy Young Award winner is still incredibly nasty. He throws four pitches: a four-seam fastball, changeup, slider, and curveball. His fastball and changeup break in toward a left-handed hitter, while his slider and curveball break away. His fastball has elite "ride," staying up as it reaches the plate, while his curveball drops off the table.

His arsenal is pretty standard; he doesn't throw anything exotic like Yamamoto's splitter. Still, he remains one of the best pitchers in the game for a few reasons:

1. All of his pitches are swing-and-miss pitches: Most starters have one or two put-away pitches, but all four of Snell's miss bats. His curveball is probably his best pitch and one of the best breaking balls in the game.

Snell has missed chunks of the last three seasons due to injury, so he hasn't qualified for year-end leaderboards since 2023, his second Cy Young season. That year, all three of his secondary pitches (slider, changeup, and curveball) had whiff rates around 50%, and his overall whiff rate ranked in the 98th percentile.

2. His fastball-curveball combination is brutal: In Game 3, his four-seamer sat around 97-98 mph with about 18-20 inches of induced vertical break, meaning it rode higher than hitters expected. His curveball came in around 83 mph and dropped roughly four feet. Both come from the same arm slot, so hitters have to guess between a fastball riding up at the letters and a curveball that falls off the table and out of the bottom of the zone. On top of that, the curveball arrives about 15 mph slower, so even a hitter who guesses right on location can be way out in front.

3. He works the edges of the zone: Snell rarely gives in with something over the middle. He lives on the corners and just above and below the zone, which leads to lots of chases and weak contact when hitters do swing.

The tradeoff is that he's more prone to walks and high pitch counts than your average ace. His approach would rather put a hitter on base than give him something to drive. A few more stats from his 2023 season:

Only 44.7% of his fastballs were in the strike zone, the 14th-lowest rate among starters.

His slider had the lowest zone rate of any qualifying starter, at 25%.

In short, Snell has some of the best stuff in baseball, and he doesn't like giving hitters anything to hit. That makes what Bauers did all the more impressive:

Pitchers tend to attack Bauers up and in. He's a patient hitter, but like many power hitters, he'll hunt inside fastballs and try to drive them, which means he can sometimes be jammed or beaten by velocity. Because of that, opponents often pair high, inside fastballs with breaking balls and changeups away, trying to keep him off balance and induce weak contact. Snell was no exception.

Jake Bauers vs. Blake Snell: The Breakdown

Pitch 1: 89.4-mph slider (0-1): Snell's first pitch, a slider, starts up and in. It comes in looking like a fastball, but instead of riding up like his four-seamer, it drops late. Unlike a typical slider, though, this one has almost no horizontal break, so it doesn't sweep away from the left-handed Bauers. He initially looks like he wants it but checks his swing, presumably because he recognizes the late drop and knows he can't drive it. The slider stays in the zone for strike one.

Pitch 2: 83.8-mph changeup (1-1): Snell follows with a changeup, about 14 mph slower than his fastball, that dives 34 inches and runs in toward Bauers. Lefties don't often throw changeups to left-handed hitters (in particular, Snell's changeup performs better against righties), so it's a sign Snell is willing to show Bauers everything. The goal is to stop him from sitting on the fastball, but the pitch bounces in the dirt for ball one.

Pitch 3: 96.3-mph fastball (2-1): Snell throws a fastball low and away, likely hoping Bauers will take it for strike two so he can go for the put-away pitch. He misses, though, and the count goes to 2-1.

Pitch 4: 87.0-mph changeup (2-2): Snell comes back with another changeup, this one starting high and inside before dropping. Bauers is out in front and just barely ticks the top of the ball for a foul tip that ends up in the glove of catcher Will Smith. Strike two.

Pitch 5: 90.6-mph slider (2-2) : Snell goes back to the slider for the first time since the opening pitch. Like that first one, it has almost no horizontal break, so out of the hand it looks like a fastball, and Bauers appears to be sitting on one. His front foot comes down well before the pitch arrives, but he does a great job keeping his weight back and waiting on the slider before fouling it off to stay alive.

Pitch 6: 82.3-mph curveball (2-2) : Bauers is still a little out in front, since he's clearly not expecting a curveball, but he manages to chop it foul.

Pitch 7: 97.6-mph fastball (3-2): Snell follows the slow curveball with the hardest fastball he's thrown Bauers all at-bat, a jump of 15 mph. Bauers wants it and starts to swing, but he recognizes it's a few inches off the inside corner and checks his swing to run the count full.

Pitch 8: 98.2-mph fastball (3-2) : Snell comes back with another fastball, this one even harder than the last one. It starts up in the zone before riding up and out of it. Bauers is already committed and can't check his swing, but he gets enough of it to foul it back and stay alive.

Pitch 9: 86.3-mph changeup (3-2): Snell changes speeds again, coming back with a changeup that's about 12 mph slower than the fastball. Once again, Bauers isn't sitting on the changeup, so he's out in front, but he manages to keep his weight back and just gets a piece of it.

Pitch 10: 90.9-mph slider (3-2): Snell comes back with a third slider. Bauers is out in front again, so his swing is still awkward, but now that he's seen it a couple of times, he's able to do more than just foul it off. Bauers lines it down the right field line, but it goes just foul.

Pitch 11: 97.8-mph fastball (home run): After two straight secondary pitches, Snell goes back to the fastball, presumably trying to blow it by Bauers high and inside. Instead, it runs out over the middle of the plate, and Bauers — who's been sitting fastball all at-bat — doesn't miss it: 109.4 mph off the bat, 412 feet to right field. The two-run homer scores Christian Yelich and gives the Brewers a lead they never relinquish.

So, to correct myself: Bauers' walk against Yamamoto was the best at-bat of the NLCS for exactly one game. I'm done making predictions. (That said, at this rate, he might top this one too.)

articles.title: Man City defender Marc Guehi questions impact of taking the knee in anti-racism campaign
articles.summary: Manchester City defender Marc Guehi has questioned whether taking the knee still has the same impact as an anti-racism message after choosing to stand before...
articles.body:
Manchester City defender Marc Guehi has questioned whether taking the knee still has the same impact as an anti-racism message after choosing to stand before Saturday's Premier League victory over Ipswich Town.

Guehi was among several players who did not take part in the gesture during the league's latest "No Room For Racism" campaign.

Ipswich defender Issa Diop also remained standing, while Leeds United striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin and other players made similar decisions at their respective matches.

After City's 3-2 win over Ipswich, Guehi said he had stopped taking the knee some time ago but still supported the message behind the campaign.

"I've not been taking the knee for a while now," Guehi said (via Daily Mail ).

"I'll always clap just because of what it signifies. But in terms of if something can be done? Hopefully. Hopefully we can do a bit more, but we will see.

"More can be done. More can always be done. We'll have to see how we move the campaign along.

"I don't think it's necessarily a football issue, I think it's a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out.

"We'll try, hopefully with the PFA and the league, to see what can be done."

The debate also attracted attention at Elland Road on Sunday, where sections of the crowd booed as Leeds and Manchester United players took the knee before their 1-1 draw.

Calvert-Lewin, who netted the equaliser for Leeds, refused to take the knee and manager Daniel Farke defended the striker's decision.

"Every individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way," he said. "Defending the forward after his goal earned Leeds a 1-1 draw at Elland Road.

"It's definitely a good campaign and a good topic that football and sports, in general, support situations like this because a dressing room is a perfect example of how we should all live together.

"Different passports, different languages, different religions, but they are all together as human beings and friends who work together toward one target. This is how the world should be."

articles.title: Saints look to take skid-ending performance at Giants into success overseas
articles.summary: NEW ORLEANS (AP) — New Orleans Saints safety Justin Reid said he had trouble sleeping on the team's overnight flight from New York to Paris.“I’m not in a bad...
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS (AP) — New Orleans Saints safety Justin Reid said he had trouble sleeping on the team's overnight flight from New York to Paris.

"I'm not in a bad mood about it because you still get to ride that high off of a big-time win," Reid said Monday, alluding to the Saints' 34-27, Week 6 victory over the Giants on Sunday . "We're giving ourselves an opportunity here and able to ride on some good vibes."

After falling behind 10-0, the Saints (2-4) remarkably scored 34 straight points before holding on with a fourth down stop on a pass to the end zone, ending New York's comeback bid.

"The most important thing is that you got the win. This league is measured in wins and losses; it's not measured in scores," Reid said. "We showed up to the plate when we needed to and were able to close out a tough game."

The victory, which stopped a three-game skid, provided some respite from an increasing sense of desperation that had owner Gayle Benson expressing dissatisfaction last week.

The Saints now have a 2-1 record on the road, where their only loss came by a single point in overtime.

Next, they'll try to take a winning performance in the Big Apple into another in the City of Lights. They'll serve as the "home" team this coming Sunday in what also is the NFL's first scheduled regular-season game in France .

France sold its Louisiana territories — named to honor former French king Louis 14th — to the United States in the early 1800s. The fleur-de-lis on the Saints' helmet, as well as similar ones on the flags of New Orleans and Louisiana, resemble what was the primary emblem of French royalty for centuries.

That symbol doesn't always engender pride among modern French citizens. They live in a republic that emerged from the French Revolution in the late 1700s.

But if French spectators opt to root for the "visiting" Pittsburgh Steelers — with whom they're bound to be more familiar, given their eight Super Bowl appearances, and six championships — that might not be such a bad thing for the Saints, considering their form in front of hostile crowds this season.

The Saints' running game, which had been anemic in recent weeks, came alive against the Giants. New Orleans finished with a season-high 175 yards rushing, led by Kendre Miller's 70 yards on 20 carries. Alvin Kamara, CJ Donaldson and quarterback Tyler Shough each also ran for 30-plus yards.

"It was all 11 — physical up front," Saints coach Kellen Moore said Monday, noting that even receivers did well getting out to block Giants safeties.

"Our running backs ran really, really hard," Moore said. "We had a good mix there. We've got to continue that. We've got to build on that."

The Saints have largely done well against the pass this season, but had a rough day against the Giants, who gained 395 yards through the air.

Defensive back Martin Emerson, who grew up about a three-hour's drive east of New Orleans, in the Pensacola, Florida, area. Now in his first season with New Orleans (after his first three in Cleveland), Emerson had his first two interceptions as a Saint.

Kamara's 69 yards from scrimmage included a weaving, 31-yard touchdown on a screen pass that resembled the 31-year-old running back's vintage form.

Rookie guard Jeremiah Wright, a fourth-round draft choice out of Auburn, had his first extended playing time, subbing in on the right side when veteran Cesar Ruiz was injured.

"Proud of him for stepping up and taking advantage of the opportunity," Moore said of Wright. "You never know when your opportunity's going to present itself and you've got to take advantage of it. So, good job by him."

With backup QBs under center for the Giants, Saints cornerbacks Kool-Aid McKinstry and Quincy Riley had a difficult day — perhaps their worst this season — against receivers Malik Nabers (12 catches, 165 yards) and Isaiah Likely (six catches, 99 yards and a TD).

Ruiz left late in the first half against the Giants with a knee injury. ... The Saints still await the debut of their first-round draft choice, Jordyn Tyson , who began the season on injured reserve with a hamstring injury. He has traveled with the team to Paris in the event he is able to return to practice this week.

3:57 — The amount of time off the game clock — from 1:18 left in the second quarter until 12:21 remained in the third — it took for the Saints to turn a 10-0 deficit into a 17-10 lead.

The Saints are spending all week in Paris as they prepare for Sunday's game at the Stade de France. After that, they'll return home on a bye week and return to their recent house of horrors — the Superdome — the week after Halloween, on Nov. 8 against Cleveland.
